chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Al-Qabalah is that one comes to the barren land and takes possession of it from its owners for twenty years, or less than that, or more.' He cultivates it and pays what comes out of it (as rent/share). He said: 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.اَلْأَرْضَ اَلْخَرِبَةَ: Al-Ard al-Kharibah: Barren or uncultivated land that needs development.
key_terms.اَلْقَبَالَةُ: Al-Qabalah: A specific type of agricultural partnership or land lease contract.
key_terms.يَعْمُرُهَا: Ya'muruhā: He cultivates/develops it (improving the land's productivity).
key_terms.يُؤَدِّي مَا خَرَجَ عَلَيْهَا: Yu'addī mā kharaja 'alayhā: He pays what comes out of it (the produce or rent).

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and ruling of the agricultural contract Al-Qabalah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* defines *Al-Qabalah* as a land reclamation partnership where a cultivator takes possession of barren land (*al-ard al-khariba*) from its owner for a fixed term, typically twenty years, to cultivate it in exchange for a share of the produce. The Imam’s declaration of permissibility (*la ba'sa*) underscores the validity of this contract in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the principle that the effort of cultivation justifies the cultivator's claim to the yield, thereby encouraging agricultural development and land utilization.
